chunks: Among the signs of anyone of them is that you will see that he has strength in religion,

determination along with leniency, faith with conviction, eagerness for knowledge, and knowledge with forbearance, moderation in riches, devotion in worship, gracefulness in starvation, endurance in hardship, desire for the lawful, pleasure in guidance and hatred from greed.

He performs virtuous deeds but still feels afraid. In the evening he is anxious to offer thanks (to Allāh). In the morning his anxiety is to remember (Allāh). He passes the night in fear and rises in the morning in joy - fear lest night is passed in forgetfulness, and joy over the favour and mercy received by him.
If his self refuses to endure a thing which it does not like he does not grant its request towards what it likes.
The coolness of his eye lies in what is to last for ever, while from the things (of this world) that will not last he keeps aloof. He transfuses knowledge with forbearance, and speech with action.
ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual and ethical signs of a God-fearing person according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha, often cited in Shia scholarship as a description of the *Muttaqin* (God-fearing) or specifically Imam Ali himself, emphasizes the dialectical balance of virtues where strength is tempered with gentleness and knowledge with humility. It underscores the practical discipline of the soul (*jihad al-nafs*), illustrating how the righteous maintain a state of joyful vigilance by combining fear of heedlessness with gratitude for divine grace. This synthesis of inner tranquility and outward action reflects the Shia ideal of integrating spiritual depth with active worldly engagement.
